audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. False quartic separation in the analytic continuation proof; Domain norm does not imply the displayed high-dimensional decay rate; Mass factor cannot bound arbitrary K derivative directions
limitations: P01 — False quartic separation in the analytic continuation proof — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Real counterexample precedes complex-parameter interpretation.
P01 — False quartic separation in the analytic continuation proof — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Lemma8.4 only supplies valid Jensen M|y|^4; does not supply sum|phi|^4 addition.

P01 — False quartic separation in the analytic continuation proof — Counterevidence: Mean-zero cancels the linear term in phi but not sum phi^3. The Jensen bound used later on pages 90â€“91 only gives sum|phi+y|^4 >= M|y|^4 and does not imply coefficient-one separation. Source Lemma 2.1 feeds Corollary 2.2 and the central moment identities; this is a false step in a core derivation, not a demonstration that the moment identities or final scaling laws are false.
P02 — Domain norm does not imply the displayed high-dimensional decay rate — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Test functions are domain elements, not asserted actual RG trajectory fromK0=0.
P02 — Domain norm does not imply the displayed high-dimensional decay rate — Counterevidence and alternative readings: g/gtilde bounded comparison cannot repair exponential discrepancy.
P02 — Domain norm does not imply the displayed high-dimensional decay rate — Counterevidence and alternative readings: epsilon0 is prohibited by strictcontraction margin.

P02 — Domain norm does not imply the displayed high-dimensional decay rate — Counterevidence: This disproves the asserted domain implication; it does not claim the specially initialized RG trajectory K_0=0 realizes the counterexample. An additional trajectory estimate could repair the gap, but is not provided by domain membership. Epsilon cannot simply be set to zero: source (9.4),(9.23) use the strict margins to absorb L-dependent constants. With the explicit epsilon=1/(2d-6), the domain decay exponents are 17/3 at d=12 and 247/40 at d=13, weaker than respectively 6 and 13/2 claimed for e_N.
P03 — Mass factor cannot bound arbitrary K derivative directions — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Own(9.35),(9.39),(9.40),(9.43),(9.44) leave lambdaK outside massfactor.
P03 — Mass factor cannot bound arbitrary K derivative directions — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Bookphysical166 equation10.4.26 leaves lambdaK outside factor.
P03 — Mass factor cannot bound arbitrary K derivative directions — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Theorem9.1 general q>=1 doesnotneedtheta;crucial q1 contractionseparate.

P03 — Mass factor cannot bound arbitrary K derivative directions — Counterevidence: The source's own estimates (9.35),(9.39),(9.40),(9.43),(9.44) on pages 104â€“105 put lambda_K outside the theta factor. The independently read and viewed reference-book (10.4.26), printed page 156, likewise has (theta^3 g^3+lambda_K)g^(-9/4). Theorem 9.1 distinguishes zero-K-derivative estimates from general K derivatives, and the special contraction case has its separate Proposition 9.5. The report identifies a false bound in a central RG estimate without claiming the full final scaling conclusions are false.
P04 — Introductory susceptibility equivalence lacks a logarithmic growth restriction — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Theorem1.2 sN<=L^sqrtN satisfiesmissinglog sN=oN.
P04 — Introductory susceptibility equivalence lacks a logarithmic growth restriction — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Section1.5notusedmainproof.

P04 — Introductory susceptibility equivalence lacks a logarithmic growth restriction — Counterevidence: The actual positive scaling-window range of Theorem 1.2 is at most L^(sqrt(N)) in the d=4 case checked; it satisfies log s_N=o(N). Section 1.5 explicitly says this introductory comparison is not used in the core proof. The issue therefore does not invalidate the stated proved scaling range.
P05 — Covariance lemma overstates the arbitrary-degree field growth — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Allidentifiedoperativeapplicationsquarticp2,notrefuted.
P05 — Covariance lemma overstates the arbitrary-degree field growth — Counterevidence and alternative readings: BookLemma7.6.1physical122-123hasquarticscope.

P05 — Covariance lemma overstates the arbitrary-degree field growth — Counterevidence: The application excerpts on pages 94,98,103 use quartic Q or Vhat. For p=2 the necessary covariance degree 4p-4 equals the printed degree 2p=4; those uses are not refuted. The reference-book covariance section read on physical pages 122â€“123 also treats the quartic setting and does not supply the arbitrary-degree generalization.
P06 — Endpoint Laplace evaluation has a factor-of-two prefactor error — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Reference11publisherTheorem1.3physical9 givesGamma(3/2)/sqrt(PN),correct.
P06 — Endpoint Laplace evaluation has a factor-of-two prefactor error — Counterevidence and alternative readings: Reference11Theorem3.1physical21 includes1/mu.
P06 — Endpoint Laplace evaluation has a factor-of-two prefactor error — Counterevidence and alternative readings: PropositionB2requiresonlypositiveconstants,soitsstatementnotrefuted.

P06 — Endpoint Laplace evaluation has a factor-of-two prefactor error — Counterevidence: The reference's physical page 9, printed 174, gives Gamma(3/2)=sqrt(pi)/2 for the same second-order endpoint in both G_01 and susceptibility, and its endpoint theorem on physical page 21 retains 1/mu. The exact reference representation on physical pages 24â€“25 recovers (B.7) by integration by parts. The diagonal term satisfies G_00=1-V'(0)+G_01-integral exp(-NV)V''=1+O(N^(-1/2)) on this fixed window and cannot supply the missing sqrt(N) factor. The source's Proposition B.2 asserts existence of positive constants, so replacing lambda_1 by P^(-1/2), lambda_2 by b P^(-1/2) preserves that statement. No integer-spin main theorem is refuted.

proposition.claim:
Recorded check: False quartic separation in the analytic continuation proof

N: 1. D: >=4. L: sufficiently large. N: >=1. G: any allowed positive g. Field: (2,-1,-1,0,...), zero sum. Constant shift: -1/10. Mass: any admitted real mass.

Recorded check: Domain norm does not imply the displayed high-dimensional decay rate

D: >=12. N: 1. Mass: 0. Epsilon: 0<epsilon<1/(d-3); specific1/(2d-6). Rho: L^(-(d-4)j). P: d(1-epsilon)/(2(d-4)). K: epsilon0*gtilde_j^3*rho_j^p*H(phi/h_j),H=t^6 exp(-c t^4),c>kappa.

Recorded check: Mass factor cannot bound arbitrary K derivative directions

N: 1. D: >=4. J: 0. L: fixed sufficiently large. G: fixed sufficiently small. V: g phi^4/4. K: 0. Lambdav: 0. Lambdak: g^(9/4)/2. A tilde and a: coincident, tendtoinfinity. Direction: W0-normalizedH=c0phi^6exp(-cphi^4),Loc(e^V H)=0.

Recorded check: Introductory susceptibility equivalence lacks a logarithmic growth restriction

D: 4. N: >=1. G: fixed sufficiently small. Sn: L^N. Restrictions: sN>=epsilon>0 andsN*wN->0 bothhold.

Recorded check: Covariance lemma overstates the arbitrary-degree field growth

P: 3. N: 1. J: 0. A: 0. M: L^d>1. C: I-J/M. V1 and v2: sum_x phi_x^6,even mass-independent. H: fixedallowedh>=c_+. Lambdav: 0. Lambdak: 0.

Recorded check: Endpoint Laplace evaluation has a factor-of-two prefactor error

G: >0fixed. Nu: nu_c+sN^-1/2,sfixedreal. P: V_c''(0)/2>0. B: dotV_c'(0)>0. Critical minimum: uniqueat0,tailgrowslinearly;provedforactualB4modelviaM0=1andM_k<k!.
